close_reason: Code-eliminated by the Arc-64 save-verdict Bash-only module rewrite (main 20267e4): the Python _save_verdict.py is removed, so these script-specific bugs/ergonomics no longer exist.
description: Arc 56 (wq0) shipped a WORKING Bash-only verdict-authoring mechanism for no-Write seats (ARGUS/CATO/ZENO/NOMOS/TIRO): printf '%s' '<body>' > worktree-relative-path, with '\'' apostrophe-escaping. That mechanism works (ARGUS used it live in Arc 56) but is ergonomically tedious: single-quoted printf needs '\'' for every apostrophe; double-quoted printf is apostrophe-safe but not $/backtick-safe. NOT a blocker (wq0 is fixed) — this is an ergonomic follow-up. Concrete candidate: add a --body-stdin option to _save_verdict.py (read sys.stdin.buffer) + a documented heredoc-free piping recipe, so Bash-only seats can author arbitrary bodies without manual shell-escaping. Decide at design time whether --body-stdin actually removes the get-bytes-into-bash friction or just relocates it; if it doesn't, the printf-with-escaping discipline stands as the canonical Bash-only mechanism. Cross-ref: stoa--wq0 (the arc that established printf as the working baseline), Arc 56 seat-aware teaching d7cd8c5.
title: save-verdict: cleaner fully-quoting-safe Bash-only body-authoring (candidate: --body-stdin)
